questions.stem: Which of the following data elements are key to an effective Software Asset Management practice within ServiceNow? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Key Elements: Software allocations assign rights to users/devices, software models define license details, foundation data provides base config, and entitlements define use rights. Contracts (D) underlie entitlements but are not listed as a core SAM element. (p233)

questions.stem:
HOTSPOT -
Match the best practice method for the amount of data:
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Data Import Best Practice: Discovery suits large-scale automated collection; import sets handle medium bulk data; manual entry is practical for small datasets. Matching method to data volume ensures accuracy and efficiency.

questions.stem: Within Software Asset Management there are many key terms to understand, what is the best definition for Normalization?

options.text: One or more use rights assigned to a specific device or user
The process of standardizing discovered software installation to defined norms
The process of producing a compliance position by comparing the number of software rights acquired against the normalized software inventory
Software license details that define use rights

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Normalization: The process of standardizing discovered software installations to defined norms improves reconciliation accuracy by mapping discovery models to entitlements. A=entitlement right, B=classification, D=reconciliation, E=license details. (p120)

questions.stem: Which discovery sources are recommended by ServiceNow to populate ServiceNow software installation table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Discovery Sources: ServiceNow Discovery (D) and Microsoft SCCM (C) are the two recommended sources to populate the software installation table. UCMDB, Service Mapping, and Orchestration are not recommended for this purpose. (p117)

questions.stem: Creation of a template can help facilitate future data imports and be reused to import and transform data.
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Import Templates: Import templates store field mappings and transform rules, enabling reuse for recurring data imports. Creating a template once eliminates manual remapping on subsequent imports. True.

questions.stem: Client access is the right to use for a specific amount of time.
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > License Types: Client access licenses (CALs) grant the right to use software on behalf of a specific user or device—not for a time period. Time-limited access describes subscription licenses. Statement is False.

questions.stem: Coalesce can only use a single field to uniquely identify a record.
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Coalesce: Coalesce in transform maps can use multiple fields together to uniquely identify an existing record, preventing duplicates. Single-field coalesce is supported but not the only option. Statement is False.

questions.stem: When receiving an order, which data point is mandatory?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Receiving Orders: Asset Tag is mandatory when receiving hardware on a purchase order as it uniquely identifies the asset record. Serial number, cost, and assigned-to fields are optional during receiving. (p1289)

questions.stem: How are the Software Asset Management Professional Plugins activated?

options.text: They are requested from and activated by an admin user
They are activated by the sam_developer user
They are activated by the sam_admin user
They are requested from and activated by ServiceNow support
They are activated by default in the base ServiceNow system

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Plugin Activation: SAM Professional (com.snc.samp) requires a separate subscription and must be requested from and activated by ServiceNow support. Unlike standard plugins, admins cannot self-activate it. (p275)

questions.stem: Which of the following are true of plugins? (Choose two.)

options.text: Plugins can be disabled or deactivated when no longer in use.
Plugins can be activated by default in the base ServiceNow system.
When a plugin is active you cannot hide its functionality.
Plugins are stand-alone and do not depend on other plugins being activated.
Plugins are software components that provide specific features and functionalities.

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Plugins: Some plugins activate by default in base ServiceNow (B), and all plugins provide specific features and functionalities (E). Plugins generally cannot be deactivated once active (A false), have dependencies (D false), and functionality can be hidden (C false).

questions.stem: When receiving software related to a purchase order in ServiceNow, which data point is mandatory?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Receiving Software: Asset Tag (E) is mandatory when receiving software on a purchase order to create or match the software asset record. License key, serial number, and cost are optional during the receiving process. (p2313)

questions.stem: Which of the following are NOT features of the Publisher workbench navigation tree? (Choose two.)

options.text: List of all publishers out of compliance

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Publisher Workbench: Navigation tree features are Filter products, Compliance toggle switch, Expand/collapse tree links, and Software model compliance icons. 'List of all publishers' (B) and 'List of publishers out of compliance' (F) are NOT navigation tree features. (p289)

questions.stem: Mechanism for mapping data from the import set table to the permanent table in ServiceNow is called:
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Data Import: A Transform Map defines field-level mappings from an import set staging table to a target ServiceNow table, transforming and cleansing data. Mapping Assist helps create maps but is not the mechanism itself.

questions.stem: In which stage of the ServiceNow Implementation Methodology (SIM) is the purpose to define processes and requirements for engagement and finalize delivery plan and user stories?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > SIM Stages: The Prepare stage defines processes and requirements and finalizes the delivery plan and user stories. Initiate=kick-off, Create=build/config, Transition=testing/go-live, Close=wrap-up.

questions.stem: What is used to determine if installations are a part of a suite only when the suite parent is not discovered on a device?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Suite Detection: When the suite parent is not discovered on a device, the inference percent determines if the percentage of child component installations qualifies the suite as installed. Number and Mandatory settings are secondary. (p126)

questions.stem: Which statements are true in regards to ServiceNow’s Client Software Distribution (CSD) functionality? (Choose two.)

options.text: Removes software daily utilizing a scheduled job.
ServiceNow does not have Client Software Distribution.
The first stage in the CSD process flow is configuration.
CSD can automatically distribute and reclaim software without a license for Orchestration.

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > CSD: Client Software Distribution removes software via scheduled jobs (A) and begins with the Configuration stage in the process flow (C). CSD requires Orchestration license (D is false); ServiceNow does have CSD (B is false).

questions.stem: Which of the following SAM roles has permission to grant a user the script writing capability?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Roles: The sam_admin role manages user roles and grants the sam_developer role, which provides script-writing capability comparable to sys_admin. sam_developer users must be explicitly granted this role by a sam_admin. (p937)

questions.stem: Within the Capability Blueprint there are 4 tiers identified. Which tier is identified as Tier 1?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Capability Blueprint: Tier 1 is Trustworthy Data (the foundational tier), Tier 2 is Practical Management, Tier 3 is Operational Integration, and Tier 4 is Strategic Conformance. Trustworthy data underpins all higher tiers.

questions.stem: Which of the following are available publisher packs? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Publisher Packs: Available publisher packs include SAP (A), Citrix (C), Oracle (E), and IBM (F). OpenVMS (B) and NetSuite (D) are not available publisher packs in ServiceNow SAM Professional. (p322)

questions.stem: Which of the following features aggregates usage over a period of time and specifies a minimum number of hours the software must be used, or date last used?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reclamation: A software reclamation rule aggregates usage over a time period and specifies minimum hours used or date last used to identify removal candidates. This is distinct from reclamation type (C) or consumption rule (D). (p909)

questions.stem: By default, which user role must verify the successful activation of plugins by ServiceNow support?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Plugin Activation: The sys_admin user role is responsible for verifying successful plugin activation by ServiceNow support, as sys_admin has full platform access to check plugin status and activate remaining dependencies.

questions.stem: When populating software usage records automatically via Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM), which plugins are required? (Choose two.)

options.text: Performance Analytics Premium for Software Asset Management plugin

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > SCCM Plugins: Importing SCCM software usage data requires the Microsoft SCCM Software Usage plugin (B) and the Microsoft SCCM Integration plugin (C). The usage plugin imports usage records while the integration plugin enables the SCCM connection. (p199)

questions.stem: An allocation is automatically created in which of the following scenarios? (Choose two.)

options.text: After receiving the rights for software from a purchase order
After a Create allocation remediation option has been taken
After reconciliation runs and identifies that rights are ‘Not allocated in use’
When a software installation is discovered
After successfully sourcing a request via an existing entitlement

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Auto Allocations: Allocations are automatically created after a Create Allocation remediation option is taken (B), and after successfully sourcing a software request via an existing entitlement (E), where the workflow assigns an allocation automatically. (p1100)

questions.stem: In the ServiceNow base platform, which roles have the ability to refresh processor definitions?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Processor Definitions: The sam_admin and sys_admin roles have the ability to refresh processor definitions in ServiceNow. sam_user cannot perform this action. Only these two administrative roles can update processor-related configuration data.

questions.stem: Which of the following are required to import usage data using the System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) data? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > SCCM Usage Import: Importing SCCM usage data requires a Software Product (B) to identify what to track, a Product Process (E) defining the file/platform for SCCM, and a Reclamation Rule (F) which must exist and match the import type. (p161)

questions.stem: Software usage data can be imported utilizing:
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Usage Import: Software usage data is imported into ServiceNow primarily utilizing Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM). SCCM tracks usage patterns and the SAM integration imports this data for reclamation analysis.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect with regards to on-premise import and export of Content Service data?

options.text: Clicking on the “Manage Software Library” module takes the user to an interceptor page where they can select to import or export data.
On-premise instances do not receive automatic Software Library updates.
Normalization content is eligible for the export feature.
By default, you are opted in to the Manage On-Premise Library (com.sn_samp_on_prem) plugin.
You must opt-in to the SAM Content Service through the Content Service setup page.

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > On-Premise Content: By default, you are NOT opted into the on-premise library plugin—this statement is incorrect. On-premise instances do not receive automatic updates (B is true), you must opt in to Content Service (E is true), and normalization content is exportable (C is true). (p918)

questions.stem: If a value from an import does not exist in ServiceNow and the import should not create a new record, which option should be selected?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Transform Maps: Selecting 'Reject' in a transform map's field mapping means if the imported value does not exist in ServiceNow, the entire record import is rejected rather than creating a new reference record. This prevents unintended data creation.

questions.stem: What is a first key step prior to uploading your entitlement import data via the ServiceNow-provided template?

options.text: Ensure you have filled out every field in the template file
Ensure the entitlement data is listed on the first tab of the template file
Ensure you have downloaded and used the latest version of the template file
Ensure you have the sam_user role assigned to you

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Entitlement Import: The first key step before uploading entitlement data is ensuring you have downloaded and are using the latest version of the ServiceNow-provided template file. Outdated templates may lack required fields or have incorrect formats. (p206)

questions.stem: What are three ways to get software asset data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Data Entry Methods: The three ways to get software asset data into ServiceNow are Discovery (automated scanning), Import Data (using import sets/transform maps), and Manual (direct record creation). Clone, plugins, and scripts are not standard SAM data entry methods.

questions.stem: The Software Asset Management Content Service is automatically enabled and cannot be opted out.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Content Service: The SAM Content Service is not automatically enabled—you must opt in through the Content Service setup page and can opt out. It is not mandatory. Statement is False. (p892)

questions.stem: What table is populated with the content library data that is pulled from the content service?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Content Library Table: The content library data pulled from the SAM Content Service is stored in the samp_sw_package table. This table contains normalized publisher, product, and version information from the ServiceNow content library.

questions.stem: When specified during an entitlement import, which of the following is matched to data in the Content Service Library and used to create a software model automatically?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Publisher Part Number: When a PPN (Publisher Part Number) is specified during entitlement import, it is matched to the Content Service Library and used to automatically create the corresponding software model. Without PPN, manual model creation is needed. (p101)

questions.stem: As part of the software normalization process, software discovery models are normalized via which mechanisms? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Normalization Mechanisms: Discovery models are normalized via a scheduled job (B) that runs daily (SAM - Discovery Model Normalization) and a business rule (C) that triggers normalization when a discovery model record is saved or updated. (p47)

questions.stem: What is the definition of Partially Normalized?

options.text: A discovery model normalized based on publisher field alone.
The software discovery model has not yet completed its run through the normalization process.
A discovery model was normalized based on publisher and product fields only.
A discovery model was normalized based on publisher, product, version fields.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Normalization Status: Partially Normalized means a discovery model was normalized based on publisher and product fields only—the version field remains unnormalized and editable. Publisher Normalized means only the publisher field was matched. (p959)

questions.stem: What is the name of the Scheduled job that runs daily for normalization?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Scheduled Jobs: The Discovery Model Normalization (SAM - Discovery Model Normalization) scheduled job runs daily to normalize software discovery models against the content library. Results update the Normalization and Content dashboard. (p47)

questions.stem: Within Software Asset Management there are many key terms to understand, what is the best definition for Software Allocation?

options.text: One or more use rights assigned to a specific device or user.
The process of normalizing a discovered software installation to standardized values.
Finding and recognizing software or a software feature on a device.

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Key Terms: Software Allocation is one or more use rights assigned to a specific device or user, representing the explicit assignment of license rights. Entitlement defines total rights; allocation assigns them to specific users/devices.

questions.stem: How often is the scheduled job for the normalization process run?

options.text: Nightly for new discovery models and weekly for all discovery models that do not have a status of normalized or manually normalized
Immediately for new discovery models and nightly for all discovery models that do not have a status of normalized or manually normalized

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Normalization Schedule: The normalization scheduled job runs nightly (daily) to process all discovery models that do not have a status of Normalized or Manually Normalized. This ensures new discoveries are normalized promptly. (p120)

questions.stem: Discovery models may not be fully normalized until updated content is downloaded from the ServiceNow Software Content Library. How do you determine if the content has been downloaded?

options.text: Review the Last updated date of the Central Data Service Download Status jobs on the Normalization and Content Service dashboard.
Determine if the business rule “Create a Software Normalization Download” has been triggered yet or not.
Query the scheduled job reports to determine if the “Software Content Library Download” (samp_cds_download) job has completed yet.
Review the number of records in the samp_product_map table. If there are ~7,700 records in the table, the download has completed at least once.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Content Download Verification: Review the Last Updated date of the Central Data Service Download Status jobs on the Normalization and Content Service dashboard to verify content has been downloaded. This list updates daily when the job runs. (p48)

questions.stem: When populating the Downgrade Rights table, if there is no software model corresponding to a discovery map, which of the following is automatically created?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Downgrade Rights: When populating the Downgrade Rights table and no software model corresponds to a discovery map, a Software Model is automatically created for that discovery map. This ensures downgrade rights can be applied during reconciliation. (p136)

questions.stem: For software asset management, when software is discovered, the records from the discovered pattern are copied into which table?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Tables: When software is discovered, records are copied into the Software Installation [cmdb_sam_sw_install] table, which stores all discovered software instances. The discovery model table (D) stores normalized models, not raw installation records.

questions.stem: Within ServiceNow Discovery, the Exploration phase determines what?

options.text: Are you there? How will I classify you?
What else can you tell me about yourself?
How should I classify you specifically?

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Discovery Phases: Exploration answers 'What else can you tell me about yourself?' by gathering detailed device information including running software. Scanning=Are you there, Classification=How will I classify you, Identification=Have I seen you before.

questions.stem: If your organization is currently running Discovery, but has not yet installed the SAM Professional application, what must you do after installing SAM in order to make your discovered software installation information available to SAM?

options.text: Convert the records from the [cmdb_ci_spkg] table into the [cmdb_sam_sw_install] table
Run the “Migrate software installations” script to copy records from the [cmdb_ci_spkg] table to the [cmdb_sam_sw_install] table
Run the “Discover software installations” script to copy records from the [cmdb_ci_spkg] table to the [cmdb_sam_sw_install] table
Export the records from the [cmdb_ci_spkg] table into an xml spreadsheet and import them into the [cmdb_sam_sw_install] table

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Migration: After installing SAM Professional when Discovery was already running, run the 'Migrate software installations' script to copy existing records from [cmdb_ci_spkg] to [cmdb_sam_sw_install] so prior discoveries are available to SAM.

questions.stem: ServiceNow Discovery identifies the software running on an IP-enabled device during which of its phases?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Discovery Phases: The Exploration phase identifies what software is running on a device by querying the OS for installed applications and processes. Classification and Identification handle CI typing and CMDB matching respectively.

questions.stem: When a Software Installation record is created, ServiceNow attempts to match the installation to a:
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Discovery Models: When a software installation record is created, ServiceNow auto-matches it to a Software Discovery Model, which is then normalized and linked to a Software Model for reconciliation. (p104)

questions.stem:
ServiceNow Discovery has 4 phases: Scanning; Classification; Identification; and Exploration.
In which phase is the software running on a device identified?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Discovery Phases: The Exploration phase identifies software running on a device by probing the OS for installed applications. This occurs after Scanning (live IPs), Classification (CI type), and Identification (CMDB match).

questions.stem: Any product that accurately discovers software installations on computers in an environment can be used as the source for a Software Installation data.
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Discovery Sources: Only ServiceNow-supported sources (Discovery, SCCM, and approved integrations) can be used for software installation data. Arbitrary third-party products are not supported as data sources. Statement is False.

questions.stem: When are discovery models created?

options.text: They are automatically created during discovery
They are automatically created during reconciliation
They are automatically created during normalization.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Discovery Models: Software discovery models are automatically created during the discovery process to identify and normalize software in the environment, stored in [cmdb_sam_sw_discove_model]. They are not manually created or created during normalization. (p129)

questions.stem: By default, which persona is responsible for controlling the day-to-day activities of the SAM process and ensuring the overall quality of software asset data?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Personas: The SAM Manager controls day-to-day SAM activities and ensures overall quality of software asset data. The SAM Process Owner handles governance and strategy; sam_admin handles technical administration.

questions.stem: When creating custom products: (Choose the best answer.)

options.text: Custom products should not be tracked in ServiceNow.
Custom products should not be created for anything included in the content library.
Custom products are automatically created in the content library.
Custom products should be created for anything included in the content library.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Custom Products: Custom products should not be created for software already included in the content library, as content library products receive automatic normalization updates. Custom products are only appropriate for software not in the library. (p239)

questions.stem: If a customer does not like the way reconciliation runs or calculates compliance, it is okay to modify the scripts includes, business rules and other logic to accommodate the business requirement.
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Reconciliation: Modifying core reconciliation scripts, business rules, and logic is not supported and risks breaking SAM functionality and future upgrades. Customization should be done through supported configuration options only. Statement is False.

questions.stem: By default, which ServiceNow role can view reconciliation results?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Roles: The sam_user role can view reconciliation results by default. sam_admin is required to run reconciliation or modify settings. sam_reconcile_user and sam_cmdb_user are not standard SAM roles. (p294)

questions.stem: The process of determining compliance by comparing software rights owned with normalized software installations discovered is __________________ .
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation: Reconciliation is the process of comparing software rights (entitlements) owned against normalized software installations to determine compliance status. Discovery finds installs; normalization standardizes them; reconciliation compares. (p13)

questions.stem: The definition for _________________ in the Reconciliation Product result is: “Estimated cost of remediating non-compliance based on the least number of rights needed.”
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation Results: True-up cost is the estimated cost of remediating non-compliance based on the lowest number of rights needed to become compliant. Over-licensed amount (D) is the cost of unused licenses. (p30)

questions.stem: When reconciliation is run, a list of product results displays the compliance status of software versions and editions with respect to discovery and entitlements.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation Results: Product Results show compliance at the product level, not by software versions and editions. Software Model Results (not product results) show version/edition-level compliance. Statement is False. (p150)

questions.stem: In order to write to the reconciliation results, a user would need the following role in ServiceNow: sam_reconcile_user
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Roles: sam_reconcile_user is not a standard SAM role. Writing to reconciliation results requires sam_admin. Standard roles are sam_admin, sam_user, and sam_developer. The statement is False.

questions.stem: Select the field attribute that indicates whether this product result is from the most recent reconciliation run.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Product Results: The 'Latest' field indicates whether a product result is from the most recent reconciliation run, distinguishing current results from historical records stored in the Reconciliation Results table. (p30)

questions.stem: In defining a Custom License Metric, in the Reconciliation Order field, the ___________ ‘metric rank priority’ number takes precedence.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Custom License Metrics: In the Reconciliation Order field, the lower rank value takes precedence (lower number = higher priority). This applies to both allocated and unallocated reconciliation order fields. (p914)

questions.stem: The license metric attributes related list contains metric values set in software entitlements, and is used for reconciliation (metric group, license metric, and software model combination).
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > License Metrics: The License Metric Attributes related list contains metric values set in software entitlements and is used during reconciliation for the metric group, license metric, and software model combination. Statement is True. (p107)

questions.stem: By default, when is a product result generated for a licensable product after reconciliation?

options.text: Always, even if there are no software models defined for the product
Only when there are software entitlements defined for the product
Whenever there is at least one software model defined for the product
Only when related entitlements have a cost identified

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Product Results: A product result is always generated for a licensable product after reconciliation, even if no software models are defined. Software Model Results are only created when a model or entitlement exists. (p25)

questions.stem: Which feature provides detailed, actionable information for software reconciliation?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > License Workbench: The License Workbench provides detailed, actionable information for software reconciliation in the classic UI, including publisher/product/model compliance, remediation options, and financial calculations. (p14)

questions.stem: What are the four tiers of software reconciliation results? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation Tiers: The four tiers of reconciliation results are Software Publisher (E), Software Product (B), Software Model (F), and Software License Metric (A). The doc describes three sub-tiers (Product, Model, Metric) with Publisher as the top level. (p151)

questions.stem: When reconciliation is run, what information does the license metric results display?

options.text: Results for all models and installations associated to the product
Results for all products and installations associated to the publisher
Results for each license metric associated to the software model
Results for all license metrics related to the software model

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation Results: License Metric Results display results for each license metric associated with the software model, showing rights owned and rights used per metric. Multiple results can exist per model if multiple license types are purchased. (p154)

questions.stem: To run an on-demand reconciliation, which module would you navigate to?

options.text: Software Asset > Reconciliation > Run License Position Report
Software Asset > Discovery > Run License Position Report

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > On-Demand Reconciliation: Navigate to Software Asset > Reconciliation > Run Reconciliation in the classic UI to run on-demand reconciliation. This allows targeting specific publishers or running for all publishers.

questions.stem: Which of the following features are available from the main publisher results screen of the License Workbench? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > License Workbench: The three main views on the License Workbench publisher results screen are All Publishers (A), Pinned Publishers (C), and Publishers Out of Compliance (E). Publisher License Metrics, Software Models, and Compliance are not separate screens. (p288)

questions.stem: Which related list is NOT available from the software model on the License Workbench?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > License Workbench Related Lists: Standard related lists on the software model include License Metric Results, Remediation Options, Licensed Installs, Unlicensed Installs, Unlicensed Subscriptions, and Removal Candidates. 'Unlicensed Software Products' (B) does not exist. (p290)

questions.stem: License metrics can be defined for which of the following? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > License Metrics: License metrics can be defined for Users (B), Cores (C), Devices (D), and Processors (G). These represent the fundamental units that software licenses track—not publishers, metric types, or operating systems.

questions.stem: Which license metric would be used for software that is only allowed to be installed on one computer per license right?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Per Named Device: The Per Named Device license metric licenses one specific device for a number of software installations per right. It requires explicit allocations to identify which devices are licensed. (p109)

questions.stem: Which of the following license metrics require allocations in order to maintain compliance? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Allocations Required: Per Named Device (C) and Per Named User (D) license metrics require allocations to maintain compliance. Per Core, Per User, Per Core with CAL, Per Application Instance, and Named User Plus do not require explicit allocations. (p109)

questions.stem: Which of the following are NOT tabs available on the License Workbench? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > License Workbench Tabs: The available tabs are All Publishers (B), Pinned Publishers (F), and Publishers Out of Compliance (C). NOT available as tabs: Publisher License Metrics (A), Publisher Software Models (D), and Publisher Compliance (E). (p288)

questions.stem: You can view IBM, Microsoft, Oracle and VMware license metrics as part of ServiceNow standard baseline configuration features.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Publisher-Specific Metrics: IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, and VMware license metrics are NOT visible in baseline configuration without their respective publisher packs installed. Each publisher pack adds specific license metrics. Statement is False. (p322)

questions.stem: When creating a reportable bar graph view of License Metrics, you can use which of the following options to refine how you view license metric data?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Bar Graph Options: When creating a bar graph view of license metrics, both 'Group by' AND 'Stacked by' options are available to refine how license metric data is visualized. Using both together provides the most flexibility.

questions.stem: A Software Product can only have a single license metric type associated to it.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > License Metric Types: A software model can have multiple license metric types associated to it (e.g., per user AND per device). Two metric results are generated when a model has both perpetual SA and subscription entitlements. Statement is False. (p1019)

questions.stem: By default, the license metric field is displayed on which record form within ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > License Metric Field: The License metric field is displayed by default on the Software Entitlement record form. License metrics are set in entitlements and drive reconciliation calculations based on the metric group selected.

questions.stem: What product must you procure a separate license for in order to utilize Workflow and Client Software Distribution (CSD) to automatically install software on devices.
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > CSD Requirements: A separate Orchestration license must be procured to use Workflow and Client Software Distribution (CSD) for automatically installing or removing software on devices. CSD leverages Orchestration workflows for deployment. (p199)

questions.stem: Software license management (SLM) is a key component of the software asset lifecycle. What is its primary objective?

options.text: To convert regular per user licenses into subscription licenses
To track, control, and reduce software costs, including costs associated with non-compliance findings during a software audit
To reserve a block of licenses for a specific group of users and/or user role(s)
To accurately calculate annual true-up cost and total spend on a product
To automatically install and remove software on devices using Workflow and Client Software Distribution (CSD)

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > SLM Objective: The primary objective of Software License Management is to track, control, and reduce software costs, including costs associated with non-compliance findings during software audits. This encompasses all SAM financial management goals.

questions.stem: The Per Named Device license metric licenses which of the following?

options.text: A user for a number of installations of software
A device for a number of installations of software
A specific user for a number of installations of software
Cores on a physical server or virtual machine
A specific device for a number of installations of software

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Per Named Device: Per Named Device licenses a specific device for the number of installations of software. Unlike Per Device (any device), Per Named Device must be allocated to a specific identified device. (p109)

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Metric Group on the Software Entitlement record?

options.text: To select the group of license metrics to be used on the entitlement
To select a group to see specific license metrics for a software category
To select a category of specific license entitlement attributes
To select a group to see specific license key attributes

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Metric Group: The purpose of the Metric Group on the Software Entitlement record is to select the group of license metrics to be used on that entitlement. It filters available license metrics to those relevant for the publisher (e.g., Microsoft, Oracle, IBM).

questions.stem: ServiceNow Performance Analytics identifies a trend that use of a certain software package has reduced over time. This is a potential indicator of what?

options.text: Your company is under-licensed for the product.
Your company needs to renegotiate your contract to get better pricing.
Your company is over-licensed for the product.
Your company needs to retire the unused entitlements.

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Performance Analytics: A decreasing trend in software usage identified by Performance Analytics is a potential indicator that the company is over-licensed for that product—owning more rights than needed. This creates an opportunity to reduce licenses.

questions.stem: A(n) ______________ is required for a user or device to consume software rights.
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Rights Consumption: A software entitlement is required for a user or device to consume software rights. Entitlements define the pool of rights available; allocations assign them; a workflow orchestrates the process.

questions.stem: Which of the following is required to identify users and devices that have the right to use software?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Allocations: Software Allocations identify which specific users and devices have the right to use software, assigning entitlement rights to them. Entitlements define total rights; allocations assign those rights to individuals/devices. (p233)

questions.stem: Which of the following allocation types are available on an entitlement record in the ServiceNow baseline configuration? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Allocation Types: Device allocations (A) and User allocations (E) are the two standard allocation types available on entitlement records. Country, Company, and Department allocations are consumption rule groupings, not entitlement allocation types. (p234)

questions.stem: When importing entitlements, a record generates the error, “Publisher Part Number not found”. However, the record is for an expired entitlement that is no longer needed. Which is the best UI action to select?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Entitlement Import: When an import error occurs for an expired entitlement that is no longer needed, Delete (B) is best as it removes the obsolete record. Create Entitlement/Part Number would propagate bad data; Reject is for records to track but not process. (p1029)

questions.stem: Which of the following describes Practical Management within the capability blueprint?

options.text: Improve management controls and drive immediate benefits.
Know what you have so you can manage it.
Improve efficiency and effectiveness through integration with other areas, such as request, procurement, and IT Service Management.

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Capability Blueprint: Practical Management (Tier 2) = 'Improve management controls and drive immediate benefits.' Trustworthy Data (Tier 1) = know what you have; Operational Integration (Tier 3) = improve via integration; Strategic Conformance (Tier 4) = best-in-class.

questions.stem: Blacklisted candidates are ______________ .

options.text: Software installations that are not normalized
Software installations not allowed in the network environment

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Blacklisted Software: Blacklisted candidates are software installations not allowed in the network environment (prohibited software). Low usage installs = reclamation candidates; unlicensed/unallocated = compliance issues, not necessarily blacklisted.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a core Software Asset Management function?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Core Functions: Core SAM functions are Financial Management (A), Rights Allocation (C), and Inventory Management (D). Reclamation (B) is a remediation process within SAM, not a core SAM function per the capability framework.

questions.stem: In addition to creating a new purchase order for software licenses, additional remediation options are available in Software Model results to: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Remediation Options: In addition to creating a purchase order, Software Model Results offer Remove Unallocated Installs (A) and Remove Unlicensed Installs (C). Remove Duplicate Allocations (B) and Remove Blacklisted Installs (D) are not standard remediation options. (p299)

questions.stem: What list can include manual creation, remediation options, and reclamation rules?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Removal Candidates: The Removal Candidates list can be populated via manual creation, remediation options (unallocated/unlicensed), and reclamation rules (low usage/restricted). Software Model Results and Usage lists do not include all three methods. (p32)

questions.stem: Which of the following remediation options can be performed on an individual user or device basis? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Remediation: Remove Unlicensed Installs (B), Create Allocations (C), and Purchase Rights (E) can target individual users or devices. Remove Unallocated Installs (A) and Remove Allocations (D) operate at model/entitlement level rather than individual user/device.

questions.stem: Which of the following reasons could apply when a remediation option has an ‘In Progress’ status? (Choose two.)

options.text: Workflow(s) or process(es) have been initiated to allocate software rights
Rights are now available and can be consumed during reconciliation
Workflow(s) or process(es) have been initiated to purchase software rights
Workflow(s) or process(es) have been initiated to harvest software rights
Customer instance is pending updates to CDS Server

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Remediation Status: 'In Progress' means workflows have been initiated. Allocation workflows (A) and purchase rights workflows (C) both produce In Progress status. 'Rights available' (B) = Complete; Harvest (D) = separate workflow; CDS updates (E) are unrelated.

questions.stem:
Which stage of the software asset lifecycle includes all of the following steps?
Discovering software in the environment
Normalizing installed software to standards
Reconciling entitlements to discovered software
Remediating detected variances
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Lifecycle Stages: The Manage stage encompasses the ongoing operational cycle: discovering software, normalizing installations, reconciling against entitlements, and remediating detected variances. Plan=strategy, Source=procurement, Support=helpdesk, Sunset=retirement.

questions.stem: Which catalog provides a listing of goods offered or available by a third party?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Catalogs: The Vendor Catalog provides a listing of goods offered or available by a third party (vendor). The Product Catalog is an internal model repository; the Service Catalog is for end-user requests; there is no standard 'Item Catalog.' (p2343)

questions.stem: A software model can have up to how many catalog items?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Software Models: A software model can have up to one (1) catalog item linked to it. This 1:1 relationship between software model and catalog item is enforced in the baseline ServiceNow configuration.

questions.stem:
HOTSPOT -
Define the three catalogs that support the request and procurement process.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Catalogs: The three catalogs supporting the request and procurement process are: Service Catalog (end-user requests), Vendor Catalog (goods available from vendors), and Product Catalog (model repository/asset definitions). (p2328)

questions.stem: If a user requests three items from the software catalog at the same time, how many individual requests are created?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Requests: When a user requests three items simultaneously from the software catalog, one (1) request record is created containing all three requested items (RITMs). Each ordered item becomes a separate requested item under the single request. (p2301)

questions.stem: Which of the following elements are included in Operational Integration of a SAM practice? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Capability Blueprint: Operational Integration elements include Software License Contracts (B), Software Sourcing (C), and License Change Projection (D). Entitlements/Allocations/Models belong to Trustworthy Data; Retirement/Lifecycle belong to Strategic Conformance.

questions.stem: You have a contract that is getting ready to expire. What options do you have for handling this contract and remaining compliant? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Contract Management: For an expiring contract, three options are: Extend (B) the contract term, Cancel (C) the contract, or Renew (F) with a new agreement. Reject (A), Activate (D), and Delete (E) are not appropriate responses to contract expiration. (p2271)

questions.stem: The baseline sam_admin role contains the additional roles of: sam_user, asset, and procurement_user, and which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > sam_admin Role: The sam_admin role contains sam_user, asset, procurement_user, plus contract_manager (C) and model_manager (D). sam_developer (B) must be explicitly granted separately; itil (A) and entitlement_manager (E) are not included in sam_admin. (p937)

questions.stem: What is the purpose of an external audit?

options.text: To ensure your users are not running any blacklisted software
To determine compliance with internally-defined vendor processes
To determine compliance with signed vendor agreements/contracts
To ensure your entitlements do not exceed your allocations
To determine compliance with licensing agreements regarding who, how, and when freeware software is being used

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Audits: An external audit is initiated by a vendor to determine whether a customer is compliant with signed vendor agreements and contracts. Internal audits verify internal processes; external audits verify contractual license compliance.

questions.stem: Software Asset Lifecycle has __________ components.
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Lifecycle: The Software Asset Lifecycle has 8 components/phases covering the full span from planning and procurement through deployment, management, support, retirement, and financial reconciliation.

questions.stem: Additional Software Model Lifecycles phases can be added as __________ .
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Lifecycle Phases: Additional Software Model Lifecycle phases can be added as Options (choice list entries) in the lifecycle type field, allowing organizations to define phase names beyond the standard content service-provided phases.

questions.stem: Software Model Lifecycles can only be created for an external, publisher defined date.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Lifecycle Creation: Software Model Lifecycles can be created for both publisher-defined dates (from the content service) and custom/internal dates. Admins can add custom lifecycle records. The statement is False—they are not restricted to external publisher dates only. (p243)

questions.stem: Once a weekly software content update adds lifecycle data to your instance, can it be deleted from the software model?

options.text: It can be deleted or deactivated
It cannot unless the lifecycle stage is EOL

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Lifecycle Data: Lifecycle data added by the weekly software content update cannot be deleted from the software model. It is system-managed content from the SAM Content Service and cannot be manually removed. (p99)

questions.stem: During contract negotiations, what report could you run to gain visibility to products nearing end-of support?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reports: The Software Model Lifecycle Report provides visibility into products nearing end-of-support or end-of-life, making it valuable during contract negotiations to determine which products need renewal or replacement. (p267)

questions.stem: Once you are ready to retire software in ServiceNow, what is the critical first step in the retirement process?

options.text: Manually set Allocations available on the entitlement to Zero (0)
Run the Software Model Lifecycle Report

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Retirement: The critical first step in software retirement is expiring the active software entitlements, which stops new allocations and removes the software from reconciliation calculations. This formally begins the retirement process.

questions.stem: Publisher information such as general availability and end-of-life dates will be provided as part of what feature within ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Software Model Lifecycle: Publisher information such as General Availability and End-of-Life dates are provided as part of the Software Model Lifecycle feature, populated from the SAM Content Service and displayed on software model records. (p132)

questions.stem:
A user is notified their software install has been flagged for reclamation. The user declines approval.
What is the next step in the workflow?

options.text: The user’s manager must approve or decline the reclamation.
The reclamation candidate is removed from the candidate list.
The software is reclaimed since it was not in use.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reclamation Workflow: When a user declines reclamation approval, the workflow escalates to the user's manager who must then approve or decline the removal. This manager escalation step ensures appropriate oversight of software reclamation. (p163)

questions.stem: Which of the following features enables organizations to easily upgrade a standard version of their software to an enterprise version?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Step-Up Licensing: Software Assurance (Microsoft maintenance program) enables organizations to easily upgrade (step-up) a standard version of software to an enterprise edition without purchasing a full new license. This is a key Software Assurance benefit. (p1033)

questions.stem: What role must be granted in order to create new reports that could be viewed by other people?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Reports: The Global Report User [report_global] role is required to create new reports that can be viewed by all other users across the organization. Without this role, reports are only visible to the creator.

questions.stem: Software Asset Management (SAM) Professional reports can be delivered in which formats? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Report Formats: SAM Professional reports can be delivered in PDF (B), CSV (C), and XLS (D) formats. PowerPoint is not a standard SAM report export format. These three formats cover the primary use cases for sharing and analyzing report data.

questions.stem: The goals of Software Asset Management include which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > SAM Goals: The primary goals of Software Asset Management are: Optimize software spend (A), Maintain compliance with license agreements (C), and Support software audits (E). These three goals align directly with ServiceNow's SAM value proposition. (p5)

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow plugin is used by Software Asset Management (SAM) Professional and configured during SAM Professional setup?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Setup Plugins: Normalization Data Services is the key plugin used by SAM Professional and configured during setup. It provides the content normalization capabilities that underpin the SAM discovery model matching and reconciliation processes.

questions.stem: Which SAM role must be a trained ServiceNow administrator?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Roles: sam_developer must be a trained ServiceNow administrator because this role grants script-writing privileges comparable to sys_admin—a powerful capability requiring training and accountability. sam_admin manages SAM config but does not require developer training. (p937)

questions.stem: Within Software Asset Management there are many key terms to understand, what is the best definition for Reconciliation?

options.text: Software license details that define use rights
One or more use rights assigned to a specific device or user
The process of standardizing discovered software installation data to defined norms
The process of producing a compliance position by comparing the number of software rights acquired against the normalized software inventory

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Key Terms: Reconciliation is the process of producing a compliance position by comparing software rights acquired against the normalized software inventory. A=entitlement, B=allocation, C=classification/acquisition, D=normalization.

questions.stem: By default, which persona is responsible for loading asset management data from integrations and discovery tools into SAM Pro?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Personas: The ServiceNow administrator is responsible for loading asset management data from integrations and discovery tools into SAM Professional, as this requires platform-level configuration and integration management access.

questions.stem: As part of the discovery process, when records are written to the software installation table a check is performed to determine if the information already exists in the discovery model table, if a record exists, what does the system do?

options.text: The record is deleted and recreated to ensure the most recent discovery model is recorded.
Nothing, the record exists so it is ignored.
A new record is created for the installation in the discovery model table.
A reference to the discovery model record is identified and associated to the software installation record.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Discovery Model Matching: When records are written to the software installation table and a matching discovery model exists, the system identifies that discovery model record and associates a reference to it in the software installation record—avoiding duplicate model creation. (p104)

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid on import errors (vs. after import) when using the automated entitlement import feature? (Choose three.)

options.text: Purchased rights should be greater than 0
The end date must be greater than the start date
Publisher Part Number and Software Model not found

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Import Errors: Valid on-import errors include: purchased rights must be greater than 0 (A), Publisher Part Number and Software Model not found (C), and duplicate entry (D). End date validation and PPN existence are post-import validations, not import-time errors. (p1029)

questions.stem: What are the available actions associated with the Normalization Suggestions feature? (Choose two.)

options.text: Accept – updates the discovery model with suggested values
Reject – ignores the suggestion. The next time the scheduled job is executed, it will not pick the same package or rule that was rejected previously
Save – allows you to save the suggestion to review again later
Ignore – ignores the suggestion. All fields are updated to read only until the next time the job is executed with the same package or rule that was ignored previously.
Create – creates a discovery model with suggested values

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Normalization Suggestions: Available actions for Normalization Suggestions are Accept (A) which updates the discovery model with suggested values, and Reject (B) which ignores the suggestion so it won't reappear. Save and Ignore are not standard normalization suggestion actions. (p120)

questions.stem: What is used to identify and normalize software installed in an environment?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Discovery Models: Software Discovery Models are automatically created during discovery to identify and normalize software installed in the environment. They are stored in the [cmdb_sam_sw_discove_model] table and linked to installations for normalization. (p129)

questions.stem: When a software title is transferred between vendors, the content library download and update feature will automatically propagate those changes to which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Content Propagation: When a software title is transferred between vendors, the content library download automatically propagates changes to software entitlements (A), software models (C), and discovery models (E). Transform maps and reconciliation results are not auto-updated. (p99)

questions.stem: When creating a transform map to map software installation data into the appropriate SAM table, why would you set the coalesce values for the u_display_name. u_publisher, u_version, u_installed_on, and u_assigned_to fields to be true? (Choose two.)

options.text: To ensure that you import all these fields into the table
To ensure that if all fields match an existing record on import, that a new record is created
To ensure that if all fields do not match an existing record on import, that a new record is created

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Coalesce: Setting coalesce to true on multiple fields avoids data duplication (B) by updating matching records instead of inserting new ones, and ensures a new record is created when the combined fields do NOT match an existing record (E).

questions.stem: What information is required when importing device allocations? (Choose three.)

options.text: Software model associated with the allocation
Quantity of rights allocated to the device

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Device Allocations: Importing device allocations requires the software model (A) to determine the license type, the entitlement (D) providing the rights, and quantity of rights allocated (E). Purchase order and user assignment are not required for device allocations. (p1016)

questions.stem: Within ServiceNow Discovery, the Scanning phase determines what?

options.text: What else can you tell me about yourself?
How should I classify you specifically?
Are you there? How will I classify you?

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Discovery Phases: The Scanning phase determines 'Are you there? How will I classify you?' by performing IP range scans (ping sweeps) to identify live devices and initially classify them. Exploration=what else can you tell me, Identification=have I seen you before.

questions.stem: Software models are used to connect purchased software rights with discovered software installations via which mechanism?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Discovery Maps: Software Discovery Maps are the mechanism that connects software models to discovered software installations. The discovery map links the discovery model's publisher/product/version to the corresponding software model for reconciliation. (p977)

questions.stem: ServiceNow Discovery finds IP-enabled devices and the software that runs on them. It uses a combination of the following methods to explore the devices. (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Discovery Methods: ServiceNow Discovery uses Agents (A), Probes (D), and Sensors (E) to explore devices and collect data. Probes collect data; Sensors process it; Agents enable agent-based discovery. Patterns are used in classification, not as exploration methods.

questions.stem: What does the acronym “CAL” stand for?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > License Types: CAL stands for Client Access License, which grants the right to access server software on behalf of a specific user or device. Options A, B, and D are incorrect expansions of the acronym.

questions.stem: Within the ‘Run Reconciliation’ process, how can the reconciliation be grouped?

options.text: Country, Department, Company, Region, Cost Center
Country, Business Unit, Corporation, Location, Account
Country, Business Unit, Company, Region, Cost Center

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation Grouping: Reconciliation can be grouped by Country, Department, Company, Region, and Cost Center. These five grouping options allow narrowing compliance results by organizational dimension. (p944)

questions.stem: By default, which ServiceNow role can read, but not create, a custom license script?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Roles: sam_admin can read custom license scripts but cannot create them. Creating custom license scripts requires sam_developer role, which has script-writing privileges equivalent to sys_admin. sam_admin manages SAM config but not script authoring.

questions.stem: Which of the following is set in a software entitlement and used during reconciliation to determine your compliance position?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > License Metrics: License metrics are set in software entitlements and used during reconciliation to determine compliance position. The metric (per device, per user, per processor, etc.) drives how rights are counted against installations. (p149)

questions.stem: Once downgrade rights have been populated in the Downgrade Rights table, can they be deleted?

options.text: They can be deleted or deactivated
They cannot until all associated allocations have been removed

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Downgrade Rights: Downgrade rights populated by the SAM Content Service cannot be deleted. They are system-generated and managed by the content service; only manual downgrade rights entries can be deactivated, not deleted once created. (p136)

questions.stem: By default, which ServiceNow role can run on-demand reconciliation?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation: sam_admin is the role required to run on-demand reconciliation in the classic UI. In the workspace, sam_user or sam_admin can run it. By default, the primary role for running reconciliation is sam_admin. (p294)

questions.stem: On the License Workbench, which of the following is defined as the “Estimated cost of remediating non-compliance”?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > License Workbench: True-up cost is the estimated cost of remediating non-compliance on the License Workbench, calculated as the lowest number of additional rights needed multiplied by average price. Over-licensed cost (D) is for unused licenses. (p30)

questions.stem: Automated license reconciliation keeps license positions accurate and up-to-date without manual calculations. Disregarding on-demand runs for a specific publisher or all publishers, how often does reconciliation run?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Scheduled Reconciliation: Automated license reconciliation runs weekly by default, keeping license positions current without manual intervention. On-demand runs are available for specific publishers or all publishers. (p486)

questions.stem: When reconciliation is run, what information does the software product results display?

options.text: Results for all products and installations associated to the publisher
Results for each license metric associated to the software model
Results for all models and installations associated to the product
Results for all license metrics related to the software model

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation Results: Software product results display results for all software models and installations associated to the product. Publisher results (A) aggregate across all products; license metric results (B/D) are at the software model level. (p153)

questions.stem: When reconciliation is run, what information does the software publisher results display?

options.text: Results for all products and installations associated to the publisher
Results for each license metric associated to the software model
Results for all models and installations associated to the product
Results for all license metrics related to the software model

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation Results: Software publisher results display results for all products and installations associated to the publisher, providing an aggregate compliance view. Product results show detail per product; model results show detail per software model. (p25)

questions.stem: What type of record is only created when a software model or entitlement exists for the product?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation Results: Software Model Results are only created when a software model or entitlement exists for the product. Product Results are always created for licensable products even without models. (p25)

questions.stem: For which of the following reasons could an installation be unlicensed at the Product Result level?

options.text: The software installation was not completed correctly due to an incorrect workflow set-up.
Software installation records are not associated with a software discovery model.
The software normalization process has not yet run.
The software discovery model is not mapped to the appropriate software model.
The software installation has not been fully reconciled.

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Unlicensed Installs: If software installation records are not associated with a software discovery model, they cannot be normalized or matched to a software model during reconciliation, leaving them unlicensed. Incorrect workflow (A) and incomplete reconciliation (E) are not root causes.

questions.stem: By default, which ServiceNow role can only view reconciliation results?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Roles: sam_user can view reconciliation results by default but requires sam_admin role to run reconciliation or make configuration changes. sam_reconcile_user, sam_viewer, and sam_cmdb_user are not standard SAM roles.

questions.stem: For products monitored by System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM), what usage data point(s) are imported for reclamation analysis?

options.text: Last Used and Total Usage Time

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > SCCM Usage: For SCCM-monitored products, both Last Used Date and Total Usage Time are imported for reclamation analysis. These two data points allow the reclamation rule to assess whether software is underutilized. (p909)

questions.stem: Which catalog provides a collection of models in the environment?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Catalogs: The Product Catalog is a centralized repository for model information, containing a collection of all models in the environment. The Vendor Catalog lists goods from vendors; the Service Catalog presents requestable items to users. (p2328)

questions.stem: Software reclamation is integrated with which of the following to automate the process of uninstalling software from devices and reclaiming those software rights?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reclamation Integration: Software reclamation is integrated with Client Software Distribution (CSD) and Workflow to automate the process of uninstalling software from devices and reclaiming the associated software rights. (p216)

questions.stem: Reclamation rules can be applied to what types of software? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Reclamation Rule Types: Reclamation rules can be applied to Subscription software (A) for SaaS usage tracking and Installed software (D) for on-premise installations. End-of-life, blacklisted, and freeware are not reclamation rule software types.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid Remediation Options on the License Workbench after reconciliation has been run? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Remediation Options: Valid remediation options on the License Workbench are: Purchase Rights (C), Remove Unallocated Installs (D), Remove Unlicensed Installs (E), Create Allocations (F), and Remove Allocation (G). Create Entitlements (A) and Remove Metric Attributes (B) are not valid options. (p299)

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid States of Remediation Options on the License Workbench after a reconciliation has been run? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Remediation States (Classic): Valid states on the License Workbench (classic UI) are: New (A), Void (C), Complete (D), and In Progress (F). Cancelled and Done are not standard states for the classic UI License Workbench remediation options.

questions.stem: What role(s) are required to import financial data for use in software spend detection? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Financial Data Import: Roles required to import financial transaction data for Software Spend Detection are sam_spend_import (A) and sam_admin (D). sam_user can create manual records but cannot perform bulk financial imports. (p894)

questions.stem: What type of publisher lifecycle information does the Software Lifecycle report prioritize?

options.text: Information provided in the demo data
Information provided by the software library
Information provided by the publisher pack

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Lifecycle Priority: The Software Lifecycle Report prioritizes information entered by the user over content service data, ensuring that locally maintained lifecycle dates take precedence over publisher-provided dates in the content library. (p133)

questions.stem: Maintenance entitlements can be associated with what types of entitlements (for non-Microsoft publishers)? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Maintenance Entitlements: For non-Microsoft publishers, maintenance entitlements can be associated with Upgrade (A), Perpetual (B), and Perpetual + Maintenance (D) entitlement types. They cannot be linked to Subscription or Perpetual + Subscription entitlements. (p141)

questions.stem: How are Microsoft Office 365 reserved licenses handled after true-up?

options.text: They are automatically converted into regular licenses
They are automatically disabled until additional licenses are purchased
They are automatically deleted and must be re-reserved
They are automatically removed from true-up calculations and billed separately

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > M365 Reserved Licenses: After true-up, Microsoft Office 365 reserved licenses are automatically converted into regular (active) licenses. This ensures the additional capacity is formally activated following the true-up process.

questions.stem: Using end-of-life/end-of-support software exposes your organization to security threats. What report can you run to gain visibility to these products?

options.text: Software Models with deactivated discovery maps

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > EOL Visibility: The Software Product Lifecycle Report provides visibility into end-of-life and end-of-support products, enabling organizations to identify security risks from unsupported software during contract negotiations or security reviews. (p267)

questions.stem: Performance Analytics allows users to do which of the following? (Choose three.)

options.text: Assess publisher compliance over a period of time
View trends of software license allocations
Track usage of a particular software

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Performance Analytics: PA allows users to assess publisher compliance over time (A), view trends of software license allocations (B), and track usage of particular software (E). Configuring reclamation (C) is a SAM admin function; remediating non-compliance (D) is done via the License Workbench.

questions.stem:
A user is notified their software install has been flagged for reclamation. The user declines approval.
What is the next step in the workflow?

options.text: The user’s manager must approve or decline the reclamation.
The reclamation candidate is removed from the candidate list.
The software is reclaimed since it was not in use the notification was only informational.
A justification is requested and submitted to Change Management for approval.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reclamation Workflow: After a user declines the reclamation approval, the workflow escalates to the user's manager who must then approve or decline the removal. This manager approval step is documented in the removal candidate workflow. (p163)

questions.stem: What does a usage record track?

options.text: The sum of usage for a selected data
The high watermark of software usage
The sum of usage on a weekly basis
The sum of usage since installation date
The sum of usage on a monthly basis

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Usage Records: A usage record tracks the sum of software usage on a monthly basis, aggregating total usage hours or last used dates from SCCM for the prior month period. The scheduled import runs monthly. (p160)

questions.stem: Within ServiceNow Discovery, the Classification phase determines what?

options.text: Are you there? How will I classify you?
How should I classify you specifically?
What else can you tell me about yourself?

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Discovery Phases: The Classification phase determines 'How should I classify you specifically?' by applying probe results to identify the specific CI type and model. Scanning=Are you there, Identification=Have I seen you before, Exploration=What else can you tell me.

questions.stem: When loading a large amount of software installation data, which is the best method to use?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Data Loading Methods: For loading a large amount of software installation data, Discovery is the best method as it automatically discovers, classifies, and populates installation records at scale. Import data suits medium amounts; manual is for small amounts.

questions.stem: The Per Named User license metric licenses which of the following?

options.text: A user for a number of installations of software
A device for a number of installations of software
A specific user for a number of installations of software
Cores on a physical server or virtual machine
A specific device for a number of installations of software

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Per Named User: The Per Named User license metric licenses a specific user for a number of installations of software. Unlike Per User (any user), Per Named User must be allocated to an identified named user. Allocations are required. (p109)

questions.stem: What type of record is only created when a software model or entitlement exists for the product?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Software Model Results: Software Model Results are only created when a software model or entitlement exists for the product. Product Results are always generated for licensable products. Software Asset Results and SAM Analytics Results are not standard record types. (p153)

questions.stem: Which of the following are tiers of software reconciliation results? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Reconciliation Tiers: The documented reconciliation tiers are Product Results, Software Model Results, and License Metric Results. From the options, Software License Metric (D) and Software Product (E) are valid tiers. Software Vendor/Allocation/Entitlement are not tiers. (p151)

questions.stem: Baseline license metrics are defined for which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Baseline License Metrics: Baseline license metrics are defined for Cores (A), Devices (D), and Processors (F). These are the fundamental hardware units that software licenses track in the baseline SAM configuration without publisher-specific packs.

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid Remediation Options on the License Workbench after reconciliation has been run? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Remediation Options: Valid remediation options on the License Workbench are Remove Allocations (B), Remove Unallocated Installs (C), and Remove Unlicensed Installs (D). Create Entitlements (A) and Remove Metric Attributes (E) are not valid remediation options. (p299)

questions.stem: Which of the following are valid States of Remediation Options on the License Workbench after reconciliation has been run? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Remediation States: Valid states of Remediation Options on the License Workbench are Complete (A), New (B), and In Progress (E). Void is also a valid state. Done is the workspace equivalent of Complete. Cancelled is not a standard state.

questions.stem: What are Restricted software installations?

options.text: Software installations that are unlicensed and unallocated
Software installations that are not normalized
Software installations that are unauthorized for use

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SAM > Restricted Software: Restricted software installations are those unauthorized for use in the network environment—software explicitly prohibited by policy. Low usage=reclamation candidates; unlicensed/unallocated=compliance issues, not necessarily restricted. (p32)

questions.stem: Once you are ready to retire software in ServiceNow, what is the critical first step in the retirement process?

options.text: Notify users of the software retirement
Uninstall all instances of the software

questions.explanation: [Platform] SAM > Software Retirement: The critical first step in retiring software is expiring any active software entitlements, which prevents new allocations and removes the software from reconciliation. Uninstalling instances comes after entitlement expiration.

questions.stem: After importing your entitlements via the template where would you navigate to address any entitlement import errors?

options.text: System Import Sets > Load Data > Entitlement Import Errors
Software Asset > Licensing > Entitlement import Errors
